venue.name: Big Qualicum Hatchery
venue.description: Big Qualicum Hatchery is a federal salmon hatchery and spawning channel on the Big Qualicum River near Qualicum Beach, built in 1963 and the first of the modern enhancement projects in the province. It raises Chinook, coho, pink and chum salmon. The hatchery and interpretive centre has a display room with a topographical model of the project, a viewing area that puts you level with the fish, public washrooms, a picnic site and nature trails. Visits are self guided and the site is open 7 am to 3 pm daily.
venue.address: 215 Fisheries Rd, Qualicum Beach, BC V9K 1Z5

facility_notes.washrooms: Public washrooms in the hatchery and interpretive centre.
facility_notes.lunch_space: A picnic site on the grounds, outdoors.
facility_notes.bus_parking: Please access the hatchery via River Road. Do not park on Qualicum First Nation property or you may be towed. Follow River Road down to the hatchery parking lot.

restrictions: Please access the hatchery via River Road
Do not park on Qualicum First Nation property or you may be towed
venue.hours_notes: 7 am to 3 pm daily. Please telephone to confirm holiday hours. All egg-takes are done during regular business hours, Monday through Friday.
venue.seasonal_notes: Adult salmon can be viewed from late July through to December, and the site names the first two weeks of October as the best time. Pinks run late July to early October, Chinook mid August to mid October, coho October to December and chum in November. Juvenile salmon are in the raceways and earthen channels through winter and spring, best in April and May.

programs.name: Self-guided hatchery visit
programs.description: You take yourselves around the hatchery and interpretive centre. There is a display room holding a topographical model of the Big Qualicum project, a viewing area that lets you watch the fish eye to eye, public washrooms, a picnic site and nature trails. The hatchery is open 7 am to 3 pm daily and the nearby walking trails can be used at any time. Nothing on the page says the visit has to be booked, and no price is given.
programs.what_children_do: Walk the hatchery grounds past the raceways and earthen channels looking for salmon, then go into the display room to see a model of the whole river project. The viewing area puts them level with the fish. Outside there are nature trails to follow and a picnic site to stop at.
programs.our_note: Nobody leads you round, so bring your own questions and work out the route before you arrive. The first two weeks of October are when the adult salmon are thickest, and April and May are when the young fish are in the channels. The hatchery says phone messages are not returned, so email if you want to know what is happening on a particular day, and remember the gates shut at 3 pm.
programs.practical_summary: Public washrooms, a picnic site and nature trails on the grounds, and a display room indoors. Nothing is published about a price, an age range, how many children can come or where a bus can park, so ring or email before you commit.
programs.evidence: You can take a self-guided tour of the hatchery

gaps: The address in the tracker used to point at a page under projects-projets that no longer exists. A fetch of it comes back with a status of 200, but what you get is the department's Pacific Region home page, and in a browser it simply lands there too. The live hatchery page sits under hatcheries-ecloseries, and the tracker has been corrected to it.

Nothing on the page says whether school or daycare groups are welcome, whether a group visit can be arranged, or whether staff ever show a group around. Both group answers are left open rather than answered no.
No admission price is published and the page never says a visit is free, so the cost is left blank rather than recorded as free.
No age range, no group size limit, no visit length and no booking notice are published.
Wheelchair access and stroller access are not mentioned. The directions describe a gravel road and a hatchery parking lot, but say nothing about a bus or a coach.
There is an indoor display room, but nothing says whether a group can shelter there in bad weather, so the rain question is left open.
The page carries no photographs at all, only the Government of Canada wordmarks, so there is no hero image and this record cannot be published as it stands.
There are no published coordinates and no map on the page. The point comes from geocoding the street address, and it lands on the hatchery beside the Big Qualicum River.
The hatchery says the best way to reach them is by email and that phone messages are not returned.

Fisheries and Oceans Canada runs a region wide school programme called Stream to Sea, with education coordinators, classroom aquariums and a storm drain marking activity. It is described on separate pages of the same site and is not tied to a visit to this hatchery, so none of it has been recorded here.
